title: Development Lane Handoff
description: What a lane returns to the Integrator. Distinct from handoff.schema.json, which is a validation agent's FINDING about someone else's work; this is a lane's report on its own. A lane that cannot fill this in has not finished, whatever its prose says. `evidence`, `tests` and `artifacts` are optional on BLOCKED and FAILED — a lane that could not run is not asked to invent proof — and `evidence` is required for DONE. Validated by `pnpm lanes handoff <file>`, which adds what a schema cannot see: the commit exists, changed files stayed inside allowed_paths, every verified criterion has PASS evidence, results align with the commands that produced them, failing results are classified, reruns that disagree do not become DONE, and test counts add up.

task_id.description: The graph node id this lane was dispatched against.

batch_id.description: Groups lanes dispatched together, so Reflector can separate fixed workflow overhead from follow-up analysis.

status.description: DONE requires every acceptance criterion verified and a real commit. BLOCKED is the honest answer when the cause is unclear — reporting it as FAILED sends Builder hunting a defect that may not exist.

commit.description: Full or abbreviated SHA of the lane's commit. Empty string when the lane produced no commit.

changed_files.description: Repository-relative paths, verbatim from `git diff --name-only`. Not a summary — the integrator re-checks these against allowed_paths.

commands.description: Exactly as invoked. A command that was not run does not belong here.

results.description: One entry per command, same order. `passed` is the observed exit code being zero, never an expectation.

acceptance_criteria.description: Every criterion from the work packet lands in exactly one bucket. There is no third bucket: deferred, skipped and unknown are all `unverified`.

assumptions.description: Anything the lane decided that the packet did not settle. An empty array is a claim that nothing was assumed.

failures.description: Reproductions, not suspicions. Non-empty is required when status is FAILED.

follow_up_required.description: Work this lane deliberately did not do. Belongs in BACKLOG.md as well; this field is what makes it visible at the integration gate.

token_or_usage_summary.description: Free-form, bounded. Feeds Reflector's coordination-overhead measurement without making it read a transcript.

evidence.description: One entry per acceptance criterion the lane claims. A green command is not evidence for a criterion it never exercised, so each entry names what was checked and how. Every criterion in `acceptance_criteria.verified` must appear here with result PASS.

requirement.description: The acceptance criterion, verbatim from the work packet.

actual.description: What was observed. The decisive line, not the run — the run goes in `artifact`.

verification.description: How it was observed: the command, the request, the file and line, the second interface it was read back through.

result.description: UNKNOWN is the honest answer when the check did not settle the criterion. It is not a pass, and it keeps the lane out of DONE.

source.description: Where the observation came from. `log` is a real source and never a sufficient one: a self-reported success log is the claim, not the proof, so a PASS carrying only `log` is refused. See `.claude/skills/structured-logging/SKILL.md`.

eventIds.description: Structured log records that bear on this criterion, from the JSONL named in `artifact`. An eventId with no artifact path is a reference nobody can follow.

tests.description: Required for DONE when any validation command ran tests. `discovered` is the count the runner reported collecting — a suite that discovered nothing passes perfectly and proves nothing.

skipped.description: Skipped stays a number in the report. A skip filtered out of the summary is the cheapest way to turn a gap into a green.

artifacts.description: Repository-relative paths under `.artifacts/` holding full output. Required when `failures` is non-empty: a failure whose evidence is nowhere is a claim.
